# Kapture

> Kapture is a Chrome extension that captures a complete webpage, or a selected
> area of one, and saves the result on the user's own device as a PNG, JPEG or PDF.

Kapture runs in Chrome's side panel. In full page mode it scrolls the whole
document rather than capturing only the visible viewport, splitting very long
pages into sections of up to 8,000 image rows. In select area mode the user
drags over the visible page, with Freeform, 1:1, 16:9 and 9:16 ratios.

Files are saved through Chrome's own Downloads system, into a Downloads
subfolder the user names per capture, so different pages or projects can be kept
in different folders. Kapture keeps a local capture history and offers light and
dark side panel themes.

Kapture requires Google Chrome 120 or later. A dedicated Kapture app is planned,
on Mac first; it has not been released.

## Privacy

Screenshots, webpage content, URLs and history metadata are not sent to the
developer or to external servers. Kapture contains no analytics, advertising or
tracking, requires no account, and downloads no remote code.

## Pages

- [Home](https://kaptapp.com/): what Kapture is, the two capture modes, formats, viewport presets, folders, history and themes.
- [Privacy Policy](https://kaptapp.com/privacy.html): what information Kapture handles, how it is stored locally, and what is never transmitted.
